# How to Use Midjourney on the Web: A Step-by-Step Guide

> **In short:** Midjourney's web app at midjourney.com lets you type a description and get four AI-made images in about a minute, then upscale and download the one you like best. You'll need an account and a paid plan to start.

You've probably scrolled past a gorgeous AI-made image today — the kind that looks almost like a real photograph or a polished illustration. Maybe you wondered how it was made. The tool behind many of those images is Midjourney, and you don't need to be a designer to try it. Here's how to make your first image tonight, even if you've never used an AI tool before.

## Before you start

Two things need to be in place before Step 1, or you'll hit a wall quickly:

- **A Midjourney account.** Sign up at midjourney.com with an email and password. You can also use a Discord login if you already have one.
- **An active subscription.** Midjourney no longer offers a permanent free tier. You'll need a paid plan — the Basic plan starts at around $10/month, with higher tiers available for heavier use. You pick the plan during signup, and the price is shown clearly before you pay.
- **A modern browser.** Chrome, Firefox, Safari, or Edge on a phone or laptop is all you need. No app install required — the whole thing runs in your browser.

## Step 1 — Sign in to midjourney.com

Open **midjourney.com** in your browser. On the homepage, look for the **"Sign In"** button in the top-right corner and click or tap it. If you already have an account, enter your email and password. If not, choose **"Create Account"** and follow the prompts to set one up.

You'll land on your Midjourney dashboard after a moment — that's your home base for everything below.

💬 Example: Use an email you check often, since Midjourney sends billing receipts and password resets there.

**You'll know it worked when** you see the Midjourney dashboard with your username visible in the corner and a left-hand navigation menu.

## Step 2 — Open the Imagine tab

Find the **"Imagine"** option in the left-hand sidebar on desktop, or in the bottom menu on mobile. Click or tap it once.

The screen changes to a clean canvas with a text box near the bottom. That text box is where all your images start.

💬 Example: On desktop, "Imagine" usually sits at the top of the left sidebar with a small icon next to it. On mobile, it's one of the icons along the bottom of the screen.

**You'll know it worked when** you see a wide empty area with a prompt box that says something like *"Imagine something…"*.

## Step 3 — Type your first prompt and submit

Click inside the prompt box and type a description of the image you want. Be as specific as you like about the subject, mood, lighting, and style. When you're happy with your description, press **Enter** or tap the **Generate** button (a small arrow icon on the right edge of the box).

The screen will show a progress indicator while Midjourney works. After roughly 30 to 60 seconds, four image variations appear in a 2×2 grid.

💬 Example prompt to copy: *"a cozy bookstore at night, warm lamp light, rain on the window, soft illustration style"*

**You'll know it worked when** four finished images appear in a grid, each one a slightly different take on your description.

## Step 4 — Upscale the image you like best

Look underneath the four images. You'll see a row of small buttons. The ones labeled **U1, U2, U3, and U4** stand for "Upscale" — they turn the small preview into a full-resolution, downloadable image. Click the **U** button under whichever thumbnail you like most.

Wait a few seconds. The selected image will expand to fill the main view, much larger than the original preview. The other three stay small.

💬 Example: If you like the image in the top-right of the grid, click **U2**. Top-left is **U1**, bottom-left is **U3**, bottom-right is **U4**.

**You'll know it worked when** the image fills the main canvas and a new set of buttons appears below it.

## Step 5 — Download your finished image

Below the upscaled image, look for a small **download icon** (usually a downward arrow). Click or tap it. The image saves to your default Downloads folder on a computer, or to your Photos app on a phone.

The file is a high-resolution PNG you can use anywhere — print it, share it, post it online, or open it in any image editor.

💬 Example: On a laptop, check your **Downloads** folder. On a phone, open the **Photos** app and look at your most recent items.

**You'll know it worked when** the image file appears on your device and opens cleanly when you tap or double-click it.

## Common mistakes

- **Mistake:** Typing a one-word prompt like *"cat"* and expecting a polished result. **Fix:** Add detail — subject, setting, lighting, and style. *"A fluffy orange cat sleeping on a velvet cushion, soft window light, photograph style"* works much better.
- **Mistake:** Downloading without upscaling first, then wondering why the saved image looks low-resolution. **Fix:** Always click a **U1–U4** button before downloading. The download icon only appears on the upscaled version.
- **Mistake:** Assuming there's still a free tier and getting stuck at the payment screen. **Fix:** Pick a Basic plan (around $10/month) during signup. Midjourney doesn't offer a free option anymore.
- **Mistake:** Pasting a long paragraph into the prompt box. **Fix:** Midjourney reads the start and end of prompts most carefully. Keep it to one or two sentences, with the most important details first.

## What this means for you

- **If you're a casual user or hobbyist:** This is one of the easiest moments to start playing with AI image generation. You don't need design skills — just curiosity and a willingness to describe what you imagine. Use it for birthday cards, blog headers, vision boards, or simply to surprise yourself.
- **If you're a content creator or freelancer:** Midjourney's strong prompt-following (meaning the AI listens carefully to exactly what you write) means fewer wasted generations. Spend 15 minutes testing prompts you'll actually use — cover images, social posts, mock-ups — and save your best results.
- **If you're brand new to AI image tools:** Treat this like a playground. Nothing you make is permanent. Click around, try weird ideas, and notice which words give you the strongest results. The best way to learn is by doing.

## Wrap-up

Midjourney's web app is one of the most beginner-friendly ways to make AI art right now. Pick one small idea — a scene, a mood, a style — sign up for a plan, and generate your first four images tonight. Once you see what comes back, you'll quickly get a feel for refining your prompts and making something you'd genuinely want to share.

A final note: images you generate are governed by Midjourney's terms of use. If you plan to use them commercially — selling prints, running ads, putting them on products for sale — read the licensing rules first so you know what's allowed.
